text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Defence minister Susak took off for Washington where he would undergo medical checks at Walter Reed military hospital.
- National Defence and Security Council chaired by president Tudjman says it is pleased with Croatia's recent credit rating.
- Children in state care whose parents don't visit them for over three months will be free for adoption according to a new draft family law.

- Ecology: Adopting ISO 14001 international standards of environment protection gives companies an edge in the world market, Stuart Gregory of London's Montfort University said in a lecture at the Chamber of Commerce.
- Secondary school teachers' union signs a nationwide employment agreement with the government after nine months of negotiations.
- Tourism Minister Niko Bulic says Croatia may expect up to 20 percent more bookings this summer.
- A joint Italian-Croatian committee is due to meet in Split next Monday to discuss compensation for Italian minority which fled Istria after World War Two.
- Croatia is about to sign bilateral social security agreement with Canada, says Deputy Labour Minister Vera Babic who is on a visit to Ottawa.

- Split police cracks down on a chain of usurers charging monthly interest of between five and 40 percent. Many of their borrowers were pushed to the brink of financial ruin. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
